campaigns.title: The Cabin Stalkings
campaigns.premise: Detective Mills investigates a series of disappearances at remote cabins in the woods. The evidence points to a pattern... but what's really hunting these victims?

narrative.before: Detective Mills: 'The evidence bags are scattered across my desk. Three victims, three cabins... I need to piece together what was found at each scene before I can understand the pattern...'
narrative.after: Detective Mills: 'Interesting. All the same types of weapons, all the same victim profiles. But these coffee orders... they're personal. Someone was watching them, studying them...'

narrative.before: Detective Mills: 'The forensic report just came in. Prints everywhere at the crime scenes. But these aren't random - there's a pattern in the types of fingerprints being left behind...'
narrative.after: Detective Mills: 'Loop, whorl, arch, composite... all four types found. But that's impossible. One person doesn't have all four types of fingerprints. Unless...'

narrative.before: Detective Mills: 'I found this in the evidence locker. More tools were recovered than listed in the official report. Someone's hiding something...'
narrative.after: Detective Mills: 'Swab, tape, light, bag... standard forensic tools. But these horror movie weapons... they match the MO of a killer from 20 years ago. The Butcher of Blackwood Cabin.'

narrative.before: Detective Mills: 'I'm at the fourth cabin. The security footage shows someone was here 20 minutes ago. I have limited time to gather evidence before they return...'
narrative.after: Detective Mills: 'I barely got out with the evidence. Serial, mass, spree, vigilante... the killer's profile is becoming clear. And these forest sounds... I heard them all while I was escaping.'

narrative.before: Detective Mills: 'Back at the station, going through cold case files. The Butcher of Blackwood Cabin was never caught. But these files... they contain references to something darker...'
narrative.after: Detective Mills: 'Dark room, dark water, dark forest, dark soul... the pattern emerges. The killer doesn't just stalk cabins. They hunt in places of darkness. And I just got a call about another cabin...'

campaigns.epilogue: Detective Mills: 'The Cabin Stalkings case... closed? No. Never closed. There are more cabins. More victims. More darkness. But now I understand the pattern. Now I can start hunting back...'

campaigns.title: The Recording
campaigns.premise: Sole survivor Ellie Vance wakes in a shelved tape archive with no memory of the last hour. Detective Cross patches in over a dying radio. Together they must decode the evidence on the reel before the signal flatlines - and before whatever is on the tape finishes its loop.

narrative.before: Cross (radio): 'Ellie, can you hear me? The tape on the reel - it's the only record of what happened. Sort the evidence on it. Find what belongs together.'
narrative.after: Ellie: 'Weapons, locations, evidence, the killer's habits... the reel is a confession in code. Whoever filmed this wanted it found.'

narrative.before: Ellie: 'Freeze-frames flicker across the monitor. The words in the static spell something - I have to pull the threads before the next commercial break.'
narrative.after: Cross (radio): 'Good. The spangram locked the loop open. Keep talking to me, Ellie - the signal's fading.'

narrative.before: Cross (radio): 'The box of the tape case has four sides, each printed with letters. Chain them - spell what the killer left at the scene.'
narrative.after: Ellie: 'CAULDRON... the evidence photos showed one in the barn. This isn't random. The killer stages every frame.'

narrative.before: Ellie: 'A buzzing hive of letters hums from the speaker. One letter is the core - build every word the victim tried to scream.'
narrative.after: Cross (radio): 'BOG, HOOD, BROOM... she was trapped, wasn't she? The reel ends in the basement. Get to the door, Ellie.'

narrative.before: Ellie: 'The final shelf. Cold case files, words that follow DARK, police ranks, creature names. I have 150 seconds before the tape loops.'
narrative.after: Cross (radio): 'You did it. The loop broke. Ellie - you're the only one who made it to the end of the reel. You survived it.'

campaigns.epilogue: Ellie: 'The tape stopped mid-scream. I walked out of that archive with the reel under my arm. Detective Cross says the killer is still recording somewhere. But now I know the language of the static - and I'm not afraid of it anymore.'

campaigns.title: The Midnight Broadcast
campaigns.premise: Reporter Jane receives a pirate TV signal that only appears at midnight. Each broadcast contains a puzzle - solve it, or the next victim dies. Can she decode the signal and stop the killer?

narrative.before: Reporter Jane: 'The broadcast just started. Static, then a message: "Find what doesn't belong." I need to analyze what I'm seeing before it's too late...'
narrative.after: Reporter Jane: 'The groups are connected. But what's the message hidden in these connections? There must be something I'm missing...'

narrative.before: Reporter Jane: 'The signal is breaking up - I can see letters scattered in the interference. If I don't untangle them before the next commercial, the killer broadcasts again at midnight.'
narrative.after: Reporter Jane: 'SLASHER. The spangram spelled it out. The killer is mocking me. This isn't random - these are their favorite horror icons.'

narrative.before: Reporter Jane: 'The broadcast cut to a close-up of a screaming face. Letters crawl around the edges of the frame. I need to spell what the victim is trying to say before the signal degrades.'
narrative.after: Reporter Jane: 'SCREAM... that's what she was saying. The victim knew the killer. This is connected to a case file from three years ago.'

narrative.before: Reporter Jane: 'A honeycomb of letters pulses on screen. The killer says every word I find brings me closer to their identity. One letter is the key - everything must contain it.'
narrative.after: Reporter Jane: 'CRACKER. The name of a program on the dark web. This isn't a person broadcasting - it's a group. They have a protocol, a signature.'

narrative.before: Reporter Jane: 'The final broadcast. The killer says I have 180 seconds before they go live with a new victim. Everything I've decoded leads to this moment. I need to sort the evidence one last time.'
narrative.after: Reporter Jane: 'The signal went dark. But I found them. I know where the broadcast originates. The story isn't over - it's just moving from the screen to the street. Meet me at the old station.'

campaigns.epilogue: Reporter Jane: 'The signal has been decoded. But the killer... they're still out there. Watching. Broadcasting. Waiting for midnight...'

campaigns.title: The Archive
campaigns.premise: Archivist discovers forbidden texts that drive readers to madness. Each text contains a puzzle - solve it to seal the text away, or succumb to its influence.

narrative.before: Archivist: 'I found this book in the restricted section. It says: "Only those who can separate the threads of knowledge may read further." The pages are filled with scattered words...'
narrative.after: Archivist: 'The words are connected by unseen threads. But I can feel something watching from between the pages...'

narrative.before: Archivist: 'The book grows warm in my hands. A single word pulses on the page — I must decode its letters before the text burns itself away. One letter is the key.'
narrative.after: Archivist: 'The book's first warning: humanity is neither good nor evil — merely capable of both. I should stop. But the next chapter calls to me...'

narrative.before: Archivist: 'Chapter three is written in scattered letters. I must weave them together to read the text before the ink rearranges itself. The symbols won't stay still.'
narrative.after: Archivist: 'SURVIVAL GEAR. The text describes what previous readers took into the dark places. They all prepared. They all went anyway. The archive doesn't trap you - it warns you.'

narrative.before: Archivist: 'The walls of the archive are closing in. Letters line the spines of every book - I must chain them to spell the incantation that seals the text. But which words are correct?'
narrative.after: Archivist: 'DARK, BOLT, HELD, WALK... the words form a map through the corridors of the archive. The building itself is the puzzle. Every room leads deeper.'

narrative.before: Archivist: 'The final chapter. Names of those who came before, measurements of things not meant to be measured, the psychology of madness itself. I must sort truth from fiction one last time.'
narrative.after: Archivist: 'DAHMER, GEIN, GACY, BUNDY - the previous readers. They weren't victims. They were contributors. The archive doesn't drive readers mad - it selects mad readers. And now I know my name belongs on this shelf too.'

campaigns.epilogue: Archivist: 'The archive has been cleansed. But the texts... they're not destroyed. Just sealed. For now. Another archivist will come. Another will be tempted. The cycle continues...'
